subsection.title: Solution Strategy
subsection.description: - Work backward from the approved Desired Business Impact and propose the smallest product-level approach the user can try. - Present the proposal for revision or approval instead of asking the user to design the solution from scratch. - Include a permission, privacy, safety, limit, or failure rule only when the PoC itself must honor it. - Do not assign Feature IDs or add implementation detail.

subsection.title: Essential User Experiences
subsection.description: - Propose every user experience the first PoC must not omit. - Give each essential experience a distinct name, user-observable result, and contribution to the Desired Business Impact. - Do not require a starting condition, user-action sequence, screen flow, or demo procedure; Section 4 owns those execution choices. - Preserve confirmed values, permissions, limits, and failure guarantees when they affect whether an experience is complete. - Use only user-visible or otherwise directly observable results. Do not use implementation functions, internal state, technical layers, or subjective impressions.
subsection.example:
**Essential user experiences: Rehearse a high-stakes work conversation**
| Essential user experience | User-observable result | Business impact contribution | |---------------------------|------------------------|------------------------------| | Topic-specific practice begins | An AI instructor presents an opening question for the selected work situation | The learner can rehearse the conversation that currently causes difficulty | | The conversation adapts to the learner | After an English answer, a relevant English response and next question are visible | The learner can continue realistic practice instead of memorizing a fixed script | | The learner controls the session | The learner can end the conversation and see that the practice is complete | The practice fits the learner's limited preparation time |
